Retain the initial guess as an initial guess rather than the final account. Include the exact tea-tin quotation and the two supplied quotations about mending and the month; attach their own locators. facts.text: Audio-interview record: Mira Quen, interviewed by Ives Sen; Repairing the Ferry Light; Lanternfold Memory Project; recorded April 11, 2020; https://example.org/oral/ferry-light.
At 00:12:04–00:12:19, Quen says exactly “We kept the old lens in a tea tin.”
Quen places the remembered repair before the dock moved but gives no calendar date for either event.
The packet supplies audio metadata and the described interview segments, not a separately published transcript, workshop receipt, or corroborating dated photographs.
At 00:05:10–00:05:42, Quen recalls keeping a borrowed lantern filled while the permanent light was taken apart. The excerpt does not establish the operating schedule of the ferry.
At 00:07:03–00:07:38, Quen says an unnamed worker lifted the housing while Quen carried small glass parts to a cloth-lined tray.
At 00:10:20–00:10:48, Quen initially guesses that the old lens was discarded. After Sen asks where spare parts were kept, Quen recalls the tea tin in the later 00:12:04–00:12:19 segment.
At 00:13:22–00:13:50, Quen remembers the tin's label as exactly “spare, not scrap”. The label is known here through recollection, not inspection of a surviving tin.
At 00:16:10–00:16:45, Quen says the lens was later sent to a workshop for inspection. Quen did not accompany it and does not know whether it was reused or discarded.
At 00:20:00–00:20:28, Quen says exactly “We called it mending, but I only saw the taking apart.”
At 00:22:15–00:22:40, Quen places this work before the dock's move to the opposite berth, without giving a year for either event.
At 00:24:10–00:24:32, Sen suggests that the work may have happened in autumn. Quen does not accept that dating and replies exactly “I remember the tin, not the month.”
